independent.summary: The documented invariant for the new mark is false: the comment (and the spec entry, and the lookalike test at errorShape.test.js:730) claim the Symbol "cannot arrive by `Object.assign`" / "nothing can carry it by accident", but Object.assign and object spread both copy own enumerable symbol keys — verified in this tree: `classify(Object.assign(new Error('x'), httpError(503,'X'), {status:400, code:'Y'}))` returns `{status:400, rule:'httpError status and code', body:{error:'Y'}}`, and the same with `{...marked}`. No current call site spreads a caught error, so nothing leaks today (the JSON.stringify half of the claim is correct and is what keeps provider errors out), but the stated guarantee is the thing a future `Object.assign(new Error(wrapped), err)` would be written against, and the test that purports to prove it only builds a fresh unmarked literal rather than a copy of a marked error, so it cannot fail on this.

grades.reason: Flatly untrue in the merged tree: `classify()` tests `err?.[RAISED_HERE] === true` as the first condition of rule 5 at errorHandler.js:262, which is the whole of this change.

This is the pre-fix state restated verbatim from the item description — rule 5 now demands the mark, so provider errors land on rule 3 with a `ref` and a light-tier log, which I confirmed by running tests/unit/failureNote.test.js and tests/http/{errorShape,draftFailure}.test.js (all pass, including the `invalid_api_key`/`insufficient_quota`/`context_length_exceeded` groups built with the real `openai` client).

triageGrades.reason: No authentication, session, passkey or authorization code is touched; the diff is the error-classification table, the stored failure note, docs and tests.

The change is squarely about keeping credential-bearing provider error text out of published bodies and notes, and the tests add `sk-live-TOPSECRET` and a connection-string fixture asserted absent from every response.
Spend recording in routes/drafts.js and the budget path are unmodified and no failure branch keys off the error code, so no billing behaviour changes.
No deletes, migrations, or schema/data rewrites — only error mapping and log lines, plus test-only fixtures.
The change exists because of the OpenAI client's error shape and the tests now import `APIError` from `openai` to build the real thing, so external-API error handling is directly in scope.
No version, dependency, build or deploy configuration changes; the only non-code edits are docs/api.md and the spec's decision log.
